pitch_detail.notes: Clip two bolts on the way to a ledge, then one more hanger before the protection switches to cams on the upper half. Angle out left to the chain anchor, which you can spot from the ground.
Move up and right from the belay to a bolt at the hardest move. After one more hanger the ground eases to scrambling that leads to the chain anchor at the top.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; descent is two rappels down the route, no station list so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Approach pitch: a short vertical step gives way to low-angle ice. Belay from the cave on the left.

The hard ice pitch. Steep ice leads on to more steep ice, and a roof may be in the way because the pillar often does not reach the ground. Many fixed pins sit in the adjacent rock. Belay from ice screws.
Short, secure chimney with a few hard moves at the exit onto a low-angle snow ramp. Hand-sized cams protect it. Belay from alders.

review.changed: 3 pitches written; descent already stored; no rappel stations listed.

pitch_detail.notes: Bolts only, no gear needed. The start sits under undercut rock, with the first bolt about 30 ft up, reached through the undercut or by sneaking around through alders and moss. Slab moves trend left onto the arete, then you either walk the arete or keep on slab to the anchor.

Traverse hard right beneath another undercut roof. Extend or skip the last bolt since the line goes straight over the roof and rope drag builds. One more bolt past the roof, then choose the steeper face or move left to the arete. Runout above that bolt, with the worst rock on the route; gear is possible. A thin hands crack finishes into the alder chute, where a large tree with webbing is the belay.

Mostly a scramble through alders and moss with no protection except the trees, easiest without climbing shoes. Benches of moss and alders lead to a final headwall of about 35 ft, split by an offwidth on the left and a wide-hands crack on the right. A full rope length from the last bench.

review.changed: 3 pitches written, no grades given per pitch; walk-off already stored.

pitch_detail.notes: Reach the bowl between the south buttress and the southeast ridge, as far as the moat permits. The alternate start to the South Buttress is probably the easiest way in.
Approximate pitch count. Fourth-class ground up to the upper basin; aim for the ledge below and to the left of the handcrack.
The handcrack starts here and continues to a belay in the first slight alcove.
Keep following the handcrack as it narrows somewhat. Belay about 10 ft under a small roof.
Climb through the small roof, then stem up a chimney to reach the southeast ridge.
Follow the upper half of the southeast ridge to the summit.

review.changed: 6 entries written (pitches 2-4 grouped as the text gives them only approximately); only P5 graded.

pitch_detail.notes: Begins off a ledge with the first bolt about 10 ft up. Easy, sustained climbing on good rock to the chain anchor.
Step out left from the belay, clipping an optional bolt, and continue to the two-bolt anchor at the top.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; descent: walk 25 ft right to a chain station, two rappels; not a station-by-station list so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Starts just left of the big rotten dihedral. Scramble low-angle rock to the vertical cliff, clip the first bolt about 6 ft into the steep part, then about 50 ft of technical sport climbing reaches a ledge. Move left near the top to the chain anchor.
Begins at the foot of the gully and goes straight up moderate moves on three bolts, then an easy scramble to the chain anchor.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; two-rappel descent, no stations listed.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble about 20 ft of low-angle rock to the first bolt, then go straight up the steeper wall. Around 60 ft up it eases and trends right to the chain anchor.
Climb up and left roughly 25 ft, clip a bolt past the ledge, continue by a dihedral, then scramble low-angle rock to the chain anchor.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; two-rappel descent, no stations listed.

pitch_detail.notes: Wavy, smooth face at the middle of the crag. Scramble to a ledge, clip the first bolt about 6 ft above that stance, then zigzag between ledges up the face to the chain anchor.
Straight up a series of steep steps past two bolts to the anchor.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; descent walks 30 ft left to a chain anchor and two rappels, no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the right-facing corner-ramp. Belay from alders or the rock wall. The ramp can slough or avalanche.
Snow slope. The belay is a rock overlap along the ramp, right-hand edge.
A mixed runnel with sparse gear reaches the top of the corner-ramp. The belay is awkward to build, relying on thin pitons.
Traverse right into a left-facing corner of vertical moss, protected mostly with spectres; the harder moves take rock gear well. Belay at big alders.
Up through steep vegetation then a right-facing corner, the route's hardest climbing. Protection is sparse and the rock flakes.
A few more moves up the corner, then find a way through the cornice to the canyon rim.

review.changed: 6 pitches written; descent via rappel of a neighbouring route, no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Follow the inside corner and crack to a triangular alcove, rest, then keep going up the corner to a large ledge about halfway up the cliff.
Continue up the dihedral with large gear, moving carefully around big blocks. Jams, laybacks and knee bars lead to the chains at the top.

Start from the big ledge at the base. Jam, stem and layback up to a steep section where the crux sequence leads to the top of a large delaminating section, then continue up the corner system. Standard rack to 4 inches.

Moderate inside corner on the slab with a couple of slightly runout stretches. The final crux comes where the wall steepens near the top; stem and jam to the anchor on the lip. Standard rack to 4 inches.
Starts near the stream on low-angle rock to a ledge. A small cave feature at the third bolt holds the crux move. Continue on large holds trending slightly left to the chain anchor.
Up and right along a thin seam, then straight up about 20 ft to a bolt. Easy scrambling finishes at the anchor on top of the cliff.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; descent walks 50 ft right to a chain anchor, two rappels, no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Start just right of the loose rock marking the weakness. Take the first 50 ft gently, then pull a slight overhang into much better rock in the corner system. Follow it until just before the option to reach the grassy gully, and belay at a modest ledge, building the anchor in a horizontal crack.
Either scramble the grassy gully (easy, little protection) or cross it and climb the ridge at 5.7 to the obvious belay ledge.
From the grassy ledge go right to the next ridge and follow moderate blocky terrain to a good ledge. Flaring cracks make the anchor hard to build.
Keep climbing to mossy, ledgy ground about 40 ft below a big cave, then traverse right along a grassy ledge to beneath the final corner systems.

Follow the corner system through moderate terrain that is awkward to protect, and pull around right as it steepens to a small ledge. Anchor with big cams or nuts, where the last pitch splits between the left dihedral and a wide crack straight up.

Go straight up from the belay under the wide, left-arching crack, the crux of the route. Small cams fit the back of the crack. Layback through the crux and finish up the finger crack in the corner. A 5.9 alternative goes left from the belay and takes the corner direct, but it was choked with grass and dirt.

Slab moves following bolts, then alternate bolts and small gear in broken cracks aiming for the obvious dihedral. Bolts continue up the thin dihedral to a roof, which you pull onto a slab below a grassy ledge. Small to medium cams fit after the roof.
Move right off the anchor into a short crack to a roof, traverse left through it to an easy exit onto slab, then trend left to a small ledge placing gear.

Pull up and left around the corner on steep cracks with gear, go through a small roof into a big horizontal crack that trends up and right. Follow it out, then a few slab moves up a short face to a grassy ledge. Details of this and the next pitch are uncertain.

Open to variation. A short steep crack leads to a large ledge; pick the most cohesive rock up the broken face to a finish on a diving-board-like block. Anchor is probably a slung block, possibly two bolts.

Begin in a short easy-angled dihedral to a little ledge, shift left to a brief hand crack in a right-facing corner, and follow a broken crack system with loose rock. After a second sloping ledge climb a short steep face toward the short left-facing dihedral forming the left side of the anchor ledge. Tiny gear fits in the dihedral.

Step left and up a golden face past two bolts, pull a tricky roof onto a low-angle slab with a bolt, then a brief dihedral facing left with one more bolt. Easy-angled face over a small bulge reaches a flake, steep slab past a bolt and another bulge, then a left-trending crack to a small notch on the ridge top.
Moderate terrain on decent rock; near the top move right to the chain anchor.
Up and right along a thin seam, then straight up to a bolt and on up fun slab to a bolted anchor at the cliff top.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; descent walks 50 ft right to a chain anchor, two rappels, no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Follow an easy-angled dihedral that faces left, up to a notch among boulders with fixed rappel slings, which serves as the belay. This is one of several possible starts.

Scramble over boulders and down a little, then traverse left on a small foot ledge around the north face of the summit block. A handcrack on a near-vertical wall leads to the summit. Belay from gear there, or downclimb about 10 ft of easy fifth class on the south side to the sling anchor. Could be aided at C1.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; no rappel station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble to a ledge, then place gear and clip two bolts on a smooth face with a crack running up it. The crux is short, about 40 ft. A trad option out right exists but the thin gear is poor and a block moves, hence the bolts.
Climb up and right into a thin seam protected by small gear and follow it to the upper anchor shared with the two routes to the right.

review.changed: 2 pitches written; descent walks 50 ft right to a chain anchor, two rappels, no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb a groove to ledges and a small stance below a crack rising left to right, with a single bolt guarding the next moves. Go up and right to more cracks, then step left to an anchor on a ledge.

pitch_detail.anchor: anchor below the upper steep section
pitch_detail.notes: Up and left out of the alcove to a ledge under a slab with two bolts. Climb the slab to easier ground, then a big left-facing feature with a crack to an anchor beneath the steeper upper section.

pitch_detail.anchor: on a large boulder on top
pitch_detail.notes: Step left off the belay ledge and climb a groove where some rock is loose, then angle up and right across a clean slab with cracks to the big ledge at the cliff top. The anchor is on the north side of the large boulder.

review.changed: 3 pitches written; rappel with 70 m rope mentioned but no stations.

skip_reasons.ak_lion_s_head_shit_in_the_eye: No per-pitch text: only a general narrative; pitch 1 and a short pitch 2 are mentioned, nothing for the remaining pitches.
